subject.title: Fallback turns can re-execute work already reported as completed (semantic recursive task execution)

question: Should the linked PR land as a scoped embedded sessions_spawn mitigation while this issue tracks the remaining gateway, sessions_send/cron, and Codex-native spawn surfaces, or should it wait for one shared work-spawning policy seam?
rationale: The remaining choice is not a mechanical bugfix: it defines fallback-turn delegation policy and decides whether partial fail-closed protection is acceptable before every related spawn surface is covered.

options.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
options.body: Land or rework the linked PR for embedded sessions_spawn and keep this issue open for the uncovered surfaces.

options.title: Require Shared Seam First
options.body: Hold the linked PR until one OpenClaw policy seam can cover sessions_spawn, sessions_send/cron, gateway loopback, and documented Codex scope.

options.title: Split Follow-Ups First
options.body: Ask maintainers to create or confirm separate owner-backed follow-ups before accepting the scoped embedded guard.

recommendation.title: Accept Scoped Mitigation
recommendation.body: Land or rework the linked PR for embedded sessions_spawn and keep this issue open for the uncovered surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored the cross-harness review that framed the unresolved fallback/run-boundary and Codex-native scope decision.
